action: Send the NCERT/MoE commercial-training licence request and open BharatGen Bharat Data Sagar MoU discussions
note: §19 item 1: 'Zero cost, longest lead time, highest value.' §14.3 item 6: 'Get NCERT/MoE and BharatGen licences in writing. Two letters could be worth more than a trillion scraped tokens.' §21 groups this with AIKosh contributor status as three free actions worth more than any amount of additional scraping.

action: Measure the real deduplicated Indic pool - ingest Sangraha + IndicCorp v2 + FineWeb-2 Indic + HPLT 3.0 Indic + MADLAD Indic, run global MinHash, publish the number internally
note: §19 item 2: 'Everything downstream depends on it.' §18.3 and §A.7 call the 250-500B natural-Indic estimate 'the single most important unverified number in the entire document' - an inference, never a measurement - and say measuring it 'would itself be a publishable contribution' and 'is a two-week job, not a six-month one'. Not flagged as a formal gate in the document, but described as blocking everything downstream.

action: Build the clean-tier corpus (Common Pile + Common Corpus + IndicCorp v2 + MADLAD + Stack v2 permissive + FineWeb-Edu), ~4T tokens, zero legal risk; train a 1.5B ablation model
note: §19 item 3. §4.3 calls this tier 'your insurance policy' - a 3-4T-token corpus with essentially zero provenance risk that de-risks every later decision. §14.3 item 1 and §18.2 add the reason: keep the clean tier separable so a compliant base can be retrained if the ANI ruling is reversed on appeal. Dependency on P02 is from §19 item 2's 'everything downstream depends on it', not a separately stated link.

action: Tokenizer workstream - validate fertility 1.4-2.1 across all 22 scripts, including Ol Chiki and Meitei Mayek, before freezing
note: HARD GATE. §19 item 4 lists it as a workstream; §A.3 explicitly promotes it: 'Elevate this from a workstream to a gating milestone. Nothing else should start until fertility is validated across all 22 scripts.' §B.3: 'the gate stands'. Justification: §1.3 ('your tokenizer decision is worth more than 2T extra tokens'), now quantified by The Tokenizer Tax (arXiv:2607.24276) - 8.0x average Indic tax under cl100k_base, 13.0x for Malayalam, effective context down to 12% of English, merge-failure correlation r=0.89, and o200k/XLM-R already removing 73% of it. §B.3 puts two in-project recipes on the table: retrofit o200k (BrahmicTokenizer-131K + Kronecker embeddings) vs from-scratch 200K (MUTANT-Indic / the Sarvam path). AMBIGUITY: §A.3's 'nothing else should start' conflicts with §19's schedule, where items 1-3 begin before this gate and items 5-6 start at week 4 while the gate runs to week 6; the document does not reconcile them.

action: ASR-transcribe all 35K hours of open Indic speech
note: §19 item 5: 'Nobody else has done this at scale and it produces text that exists nowhere else.' §8 quantifies the payoff: ~35,000+ open permissively-licensed Indic hours at roughly 9,000 words/hour yields on the order of 300M+ words of natural, spontaneous, dialect-rich Indic text in no web corpus anywhere - 'Transcribe all of it.' CORRECTED by §A.5: BhasaAnuvaad alone is ~44,400 hours (CC BY 4.0), and the open Indic speech total is 'well north of 100,000 hours'. Dependency on P02 is from §19 item 2's blanket 'everything downstream depends on it'.

action: Build the Indic-script OCR pipeline to unlock India's print archive
note: §19 item 6 says 'fine-tune olmOCR for Indic scripts'. MATERIALLY CORRECTED by §A.2 ('Do not use olmOCR for Devanagari'): on 300 real printed scans olmOCR-7B falls to chrF++ 40.5, worst in class, while the best open model is Qwen3-VL-8B at 75.2 on a single 24 GB GPU; build on Qwen3-VL-8B, report median and catastrophic-failure-rate rather than mean, and validate exclusively on real scans. §9 calls Indic OCR 'the single bottleneck standing between you and India's enormous scanned print archive'; §18.1 sizes it as a 2-3 month project. Dependency on P02 is from §19 item 2's blanket statement.

action: Stand up NeMo Gym with SWE-Gym / R2E-Gym / SWE-smith, plus the Indic-translated-issue variant
note: §19 item 7: 'Agentic infrastructure has the longest lead time.' §18.1 is explicit that it runs in parallel: 'Start the NeMo Gym work in parallel with data, not after' - so no data dependency is recorded. §5.2: agentic benchmarks measure a model + harness pair, so you must co-develop a harness and train against it, with rollouts up to ~100 alternating model-call/command-execution steps and a separate container image per repository. §5.3 item 3 is the differentiator: translate only the issue text of SWE-smith instances, leaving tests and patches untouched, for verifiable RL signal in Hindi/Tamil/Bengali. §B.5 adds two filters from arXiv:2607.24720 - include CoT state-transition world-model data in pre-training, and filter suboptimal trajectories hard rather than maximising volume.

action: Replicate the BhashaKritika methodology under your own licence; scale toward 2.4T Indic synthetic tokens
note: §19 item 8. §3.4 explains why replication beats ingestion: BhashaKritika's 540B synthetic Indic tokens sit under a bespoke Krutrim Community License with a model-output provenance chain through Gemma-3 and Llama-3.3, and 'the paper is detailed enough to reproduce, and replication under your own licence is the cleaner path'. §A.1 adds a cleaner option still: distil from Apache-2.0 Sarvam-105B for zero licence-chain contamination. §18.1 caps synthetic at ~50% of the Indic tier with KenLM-perplexity and n-gram diversity floors. Dependency on P02 is from §19 item 2's blanket statement.

action: Commission the private 22-language evaluation set (~3,000 native-written items)
note: §19 item 9 and §12.3 Rule 4: 'Every public Indic benchmark will be contaminated within 18 months.' A ~₹15-30 lakh project, never published, covering conversation, translation, cultural knowledge and code-mixed input - 'the most valuable evaluation asset you own'. §15.4 ranks it 6th by value-per-rupee and calls it 'your only uncontaminated measuring instrument'. Dependency on P02 is from §19 item 2's blanket statement.

action: Begin regional-publisher licensing conversations, prioritising retrieval/grounding deals over training deals
note: §19 item 10 gives 'Week 12+' with no end week, so week_end is null. §15.3 supplies the reasoning: attribution/live-access deals grew 2 (2023) -> 11 (2024) -> 18 (2025) -> ~34 projected (2026), and no single publisher has dominant leverage - 'you do not need Times of India. You need forty regional-language publishers.' §15.4 ranks the archives 4th at ₹3-15 crore. Dependency on P02 is from §19 item 2's blanket statement.

action: Scratch-vs-grow head-to-head at ~2B scale: from-scratch on your mix vs grown/upcycled from an open checkpoint, on identical data, judged on Indic + code held-out loss
note: HARD GATE. §B.6 instructs inserting two pre-capital gates into §19; §B.4 states it: 'the $1B question is not which 300B do we train but scratch vs grow - and the burden of proof now sits on scratch. Insert, before any capital commitment: a 4-week head-to-head at ~2B scale.' Evidence: LightningLM's 4-stage growth from a 1.78B dense seed to 120B on a single eight-GPU node, Grove-MoE upcycling, and §A.1's Apache-2.0 Sarvam-105B with its full MoE recipe published. §A.1 also prescribes a companion 2-week evaluation of Sarvam-105B on the target task set before committing capital: 'If it is within ~10% of your target on Indic tasks, the case for training a 300B from scratch rests entirely on coding/agentic/English headroom.' Duration is 4 weeks but no absolute week numbers are given, so week_start/week_end are null; ordering relative to §19's ten items is not specified beyond 'before any capital commitment'.

action: Indic repetition-value ablation at 1.5B scale - measure R*_D for natural, translated and synthetic Indic text
note: §B.6's second pre-capital gate insertion, though the document does not label it a gate the way it does scratch-vs-grow. §B.1: Muennighoff et al. measured up to 4 epochs of repeated data as almost as good as fresh (0.5% higher validation loss), with decay constant R*_D ~= 15 and a hard ceiling at ~16x the unique pool - which lifts the natural-Indic effective share from 2% to ~7-8% without collecting a single new token. But 'nobody has measured R*_D for Indic text, for translated text, or for synthetic text', and synthetic data plausibly has a lower repetition ceiling. Called 'the second-most-important unmeasured number after the total-unique-Indic-pool measurement' and 'a one-week ablation at 1.5B scale'. No absolute week numbers are given, so week_start/week_end are null.
